Subject: ComplyCloud partnership: secure evidence handoff & SSO mapping

Hi Alice & CloudChannel team,

Thanks again for the intro call today — excited about the potential for a native connector between ComplyCloud and Redwood that would let customers push SOC2/Security evidence directly into their GRC dashboards. Quick summary of asks from our side as we prepare a mutual action plan: 

- Basic SSO/OAuth mapping (IdP hints) and a list of supported user roles for ingestion.
- Preferred evidence transfer options (S3 presigned, SFTP over FTPS, direct HTTPS API).
- Data retention/TTL defaults and whether you can honor per-tenant retention via metadata.
- Expected downtime/maintenance windows for connector upgrades.

I'm looping in Vanessa and Jonas from GTM so they can line up partner GTM and commercial hooks. Also looping in Soojin (security) and Marissa (solutions) for technical + compliance review.

Can you share a short SOW or technical spec we can review? If you prefer, send a draft and we'll tag-team comments. Goal: finalize scope and timeline this week so we can schedule the pen-test scoping (Red Oak) and SOW signature.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Hi Priya,

Thanks — great to meet the team. I've attached a first-pass SOW and a short integration spec that covers three transfer modes (S3 presigned, secure webhook with mutual TLS, and SFTP). High level notes:

- We can support per-tenant retention metadata but need to map the retention label to a field in the payload (we suggested "retention_hours").
- Our connector expects an OAuth2 bearer token with the "evidence.write" scope for ingestion endpoints; we can also accept signed JWTs from customer IdPs if you want brokered SSO.
- Audit logs: we provide event IDs for each file and a retrieval endpoint (auth with service account).

For pen-test coordination, I looped Peter from Red Oak — they do cloud-native connector tests and can draft a scope if that's helpful.

I've attached: ComplyCloud_GRC_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW) and integration_spec.md (inline).

Happy to jump on a technical call with Marissa/soojin to align.

Cheers,
Alice Tan
Head of Integrations | ComplyCloud
alice@complycloud.io

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: ComplyCloud partnership: secure evidence handoff & SSO mapping

Thanks for the SOW + spec, Alice — good start. A few security items we need addressed before we sign off on an integration path: 

1) Encryption at-rest: if using S3 presigned URLs, ComplyCloud needs to confirm server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and give us the KMS key alias for the tenant if you will manage KMS. If they will not manage KMS, we require encrypted upload into our managed bucket and a lifecycle that denies public ACLs.

2) Authentication: the OAuth2 flow described is acceptable, but we need support for rotating client credentials without service interruption (rolling keys). Also require support for short-lived ingestion tokens (<= 1 hour).

3) Evidence provenance: each file must include a small JSON manifest (example: {"source_system":"redwood","exported_at":"...","evidence_type":"access_logs"}) — we can provide a template.

4) Auditability: endpoint must return an event id per upload and expose an event retrieval API returning signed timestamps.

I attached a short doc with our minimal evidence requirements for partners (evidence-requirements.docx). Also — Peter, please advise whether you recommend an in-scope connector test run vs. a full networked pen-test for our initial validation. My leaning: start with connector-level tests (auth, ACLs, upload handling) then expand if needed.

If everyone agrees, let's set a 30-min technical sync Thursday to pin down transfer mode and token rotation schedule.

--
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: ComplyCloud partnership: secure evidence handoff & SSO mapping

Hi all,

Attaching a technical mapping and a proposed minimal architecture for the connector (diagram link in the Drive). Key points:

- We prefer S3 presigned uploads from ComplyCloud into a per-tenant Redwood-managed bucket with lifecycle tags applied on receipt. That keeps the ingestion path simple and lets us control retention/encryption.
- If mutual TLS webhooks are used, we need to validate TLS cert pinning and return idempotent upload responses.
- For SSO: we can broker SSO via our IdP and mint short-lived ingestion JWTs (1h). This avoids giving external parties long-lived write credentials.

I've put a first draft of the pen-test scope for connector-level work in rosec-pen-test-scope.xlsx — Peter, please review and flag anything missing.

Proposed next steps:
1) Agree on transfer mode (S3 presigned preferred).
2) ComplyCloud updates SOW to include KMS/retention language.
3) Red Oak produces connector-level test plan.
4) Demo + sign SOW + run test.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
